gaps.note: Commercial break edit; may hide transition dialogue.

stage_a.note: Extremely enthusiastic, smiling, and energetic delivery throughout the pitch.
Sustained high energy and visible excitement about the product's features.
Friendly, engaging, smiling at the sharks, approachable demeanor.

venture.description: A reusable, scratch-free kitchen sponge that changes texture based on water temperature, featuring an ergonomic smiley face design.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron presents Scrub Daddy, demonstrating its texture-changing properties in hot and cold water, and its scratch-free cleaning ability.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin excitedly calls out the product name.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron smiles in response to the positive reaction.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond praises the presentation as a fantastic live infomercial.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert agrees that the presentation was incredible.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks if Aaron has samples to hand out to the panel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron confirms he has samples and begins handing them out.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks where the product is currently being sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron explains it is in five supermarkets, on their website, and on QVC.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori mentions her QVC experience and asks how his appearances went.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron says it went fantastic and they reordered 30 percent more.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks for the total sales figures across all channels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron states they have done just over 100,000 dollars in four months.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if there is a patent on the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron confirms he has one patent, two pending, and trademarks.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks what the 100,000 dollar investment will be used for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron explains he wants to set up an independent manufacturing facility.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks why he needs to build his own facility.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron says the biggest problem is being on the current manufacturer's time schedule.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks if he could make more revenue by running production 24/7.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron confirms they will need that capacity for QVC and mentions his 18 years of manufacturing experience.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks for the cost to make one unit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron states the cost to make one is about a dollar.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks what the retail selling price is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron says they sell for about 2.80 dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies if that price is wholesale.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron confirms it is wholesale and shares his vision for supermarkets.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin argues the product is too expensive compared to a two-cent generic sponge.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron counters that a Brillo pad is only 20 percent cheaper and compares his product to higher-end pads.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert challenges the retail vision, expressing doubt it will work in stores.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert adds that the packaging doesn't clearly show the product's difference.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron agrees it doesn't sell well on a plain shelf but explains his display shipper strategy.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond points out that endcaps are expensive to secure in retail.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori adds that endcaps are hard to get even if you can pay for them.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert reiterates his lack of belief in the retail vision and exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark challenges the company's dependency on QVC, calling it a disaster waiting to happen.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron counters that he has 3,000 stores lined up right now.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark states that being a one-product company is too risky and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron expresses disappointment that Mark dropped out.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori defends QVC's massive sales volume against Mark's criticism.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark points out that Lori rotates products in and out of QVC quickly.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin offers 100,000 dollars for 50 percent of the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron suggests starting the bidding there, indicating he wants more offers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond offers 50,000 dollars for 15 percent, contingent on Lori providing the rest.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori begins to speak but is interrupted.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori continues but the scene cuts to a commercial break.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond recaps his offer of 50,000 dollars for 15 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori offers 100,000 dollars for 30 percent, promising infomercials and retail placement.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond begins to speak.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin offers 100,000 dollars for 0 equity, with a 50-cent royalty dropping to 10 cents.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin questions why Aaron would give up 30 percent of his company.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond offers 150,000 dollars for 25 percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron asks the panel what they are going to do next.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori revises her offer to 100,000 dollars for 25 percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin again argues against giving up equity when the product is selling out.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if 25 percent equity is worth more than a 10-cent royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark argues that Kevin's royalty takes money out of the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori argues that Kevin doesn't know how to get the product to market.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin defends his retail connections, mentioning a recent massive Walmart deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark jokingly encourages Lori to partner with Kevin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron recaps the three standing offers from Daymond, Kevin, and Lori.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori reminds Aaron she offered 150,000 dollars previously.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron says he did not hear her offer 150,000 dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori officially revises her offer to 150,000 dollars for 25 percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond revises his offer to 175,000 dollars for 25 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori revises her offer to 200,000 dollars for 25 percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond withdraws his offer, noting he drove the price up, and exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin reacts to Daymond's exit.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin revises his royalty offer down to 25 cents until recouped, then 10 cents.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron counters Kevin, asking if he will drop the perpetual royalty to 5 cents.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin revises his offer to 7.5 cents in perpetuity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert reminds Aaron that he has two strong offers to choose from.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori pressures Aaron to make a decision or she will withdraw her offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron counters Lori, asking if she will drop her equity ask to 20 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori agrees to revise her offer to 200,000 dollars for 20 percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Aaron accepts Lori's revised offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: The panel congratulates Aaron as he hugs Lori to seal the deal.

Offers more money for less equity to sweeten the pot.
Drops equity ask to match Daymond's percentage.
Increases investment amount to beat Lori.
Increases investment amount to beat Daymond.
Withdraws offer after driving the price up, deciding to exit.
